newsitem.title: KENYA: Kabila says Zaire rebels entering capital Kinshasa.
newsitem.headline: Kabila says Zaire rebels entering capital Kinshasa.

text.p: Zaire rebel leader Laurent Kabila said on Saturday his forces, singing as they marched, were entering Zaire's capital Kinshasa from the airport about 25 km (16 miles) away.

"Our troops are marching in from the airport. We are singing as we are going, and people are cheering", Kabila told Reuters by telephone from rebel-occupied Zaire. There was no independent confirmation.

Kabila spoke after President Mobutu Sese Seko's ethnic guardsmen killed Zaire's army chief on Friday night. The ailing and embattled president had quit Kinshasa on Friday for his northern jungle palace at Gbadolite. He left his emergency-rule government in charge.
When asked about the death of General Mahele Lieko Bokungu, defence minister and chief of army staff, Kabila said he had not heard of it but it was "very, very bad".
Zairean and diplomatic sources said Mahele was killed late on Friday night at Camp Tshatshi, the barracks residence of the president.

"Mahele was killed at the camp by the Special Presidential Division (DSP)," a senior Western diplomat told Reuters in neighbouring Congo by telephone. "He went to calm the guys down and then he was shot," he said.
In Lusaka, a diplomat said Mahele was supposed to have met Kabila in the Zambian capital on Saturday to discuss a transition of power.

"General Mahele was to meet Kabila this morning in Lusaka to discuss a handover of power. It was a deal brokered by the United States," said the clearly disappointed diplomat, who declined to be identified.
